userStories.title: Register Cursor and resolve Cursor model aliases
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Register Cursor's ACP launcher and resolve unambiguous bare Cursor model names against offered IDs.

**Motivation** — nax#2372 asks for read-only support on every ACP agent.

**Approach** — Cursor registration and model ids (US-001):

- Registry entry `cursor`: launch `[local("cursor-agent", "acp")]`, `authEnv: ["CURSOR_API_KEY"]`, `readOnly: { mode: { configId: "mode", value: "ask" }, disallowedTools: [], sessionOptions: {}, launchEnv: {} }` (US-002 adds the `policy` field, US-004 sets it to `"cursor"`), `defaultMode: undefined`, `preApproval: undefined`. Mode `ask` only tells the model it is read-only; mode `plan` is never used.
- `resolveModelValue(agentName, offered, requested, secrets)` (`capabilities.ts`): returns `requested` when it is offered or the agent is not `cursor`; for `cursor`, the single offered value starting with `requested + "["`; several matches throw `AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`, capability `model`, naming every match passed through `cleanLabel(id, secrets, …)`; no match returns `requested` (the existing refusal follows). `applyModel` calls it with the config-option values of category `model` when any are offered, else with the legacy model ids.

Integration targets:
- `AcpAgentName` — Baseline: `"claude" | "codex" | "gemini" | "opencode" | "pi"`. Target: adds `"cursor"`; `ACP_AGENT_NAMES` lists it after `"codex"`.
- `applyModel` (`open.ts`) — Target: resolves the requested model through `resolveModelValue` before the config-option and legacy lookups.

Add `"cursor"` to `AcpAgentName`, the options schema's agent enum and the registry (launch `cursor-agent acp`, auth `CURSOR_API_KEY`, read-only mode `ask`, no default mode, no pre-approval). Add `resolveModelValue` to `capabilities.ts` and apply it in `applyModel` for config-option and legacy model offers. Export `CURSOR_CONFIG_OPTIONS` from the fake agent's script module.

`packages/nax-agent-acp/test/unit/client/registry.test.ts` — the test asserting ACP_AGENT_NAMES equals the five current names gains cursor after codex; a cursor entry test is added.
`packages/nax-agent-acp/test/node/registry.test.ts` — the vitest assertion that ACP_AGENT_NAMES has length 5 becomes length 6.
`packages/nax-agent-acp/test/fixtures/fake-agent/script.ts` — exports CURSOR_CONFIG_OPTIONS: a mode option (values agent, plan, ask) and a model option (values default[], claude-sonnet-5-5[context=300k,reasoning_effort=high], claude-sonnet-5-5[context=300k,reasoning_effort=low], gpt-5.5[context=272k,reasoning=medium]); no existing export changes.

The seam ACs enter at `createAgentSession` with `acpBackend({ agent: "cursor", model })` and assert the recorded `session/set_config_option` / `session/set_model` value. Use `_acpBackendDeps.launch` with the in-memory fake, never a real adapter; inspect process kill counts on failed opens.

**Scope** — In: ACP Cursor registration, auth env allowlisting, Cursor-only model alias resolution, option fixture and existing registry/legacy-model regressions. Out: rule/stateDir schema and policy selector (US-002), shell adjudication (US-003), actual Cursor policy files/pi enforcement (US-004), nax registry forwarding/docs (US-005), public argv matcher exports (US-006). Cursor persisting the selected model as its default in the operator's own `~/.cursor` under profiles `full` and `ask`. Pricing for Cursor model ids.

**Interface** — `resolveModelValue(agentName, offered, requested, secrets)` (`capabilities.ts`); `AcpAgentName` gains `"cursor"`; `ACP_AGENT_NAMES` lists it after `"codex"`. The helper consumes agentName/requested strings, readonly offered IDs and secrets, and returns the chosen model string or the specified AgentSessionError. Ambiguous-match ids in the refusal message go through cleanLabel with the session secrets, as offeredModels does.

userStories.title: Accept ACP rules and translate opencode read-tool denies
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add validated ACP permission rules and state storage options, then apply opencode read-tool deny translation at every launch.

**Motivation** — The operator asked that read-only enforcement be configurable rather than a fixed harness, and nax already has the configuration surface: `resolvePermissions` turns `execution.permissions.<stage>` into `toolGrants`, `denyRules` and `askRules` on `ResolvedPermissions`, which every `OpenSessionOpts` carries, but the ACP path reads only the resolved mode.

**Approach** — Module `packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/rule-policy.ts` (US-002, extended by US-004):

`policyLaunchEnv` returns `launchEnvFor(profile, entry)` unchanged for profiles `full` and `ask`, for entries whose `readOnly.policy` is `undefined`, and for custom agents. Otherwise it dispatches on `readOnly.policy`.

**Read-tool deny translation** (profiles `read` and `review`; under `none` the rules are ignored). Only an unconditional deny (`patterns: ["*"]`) of `Read`, `Glob` or `Grep` is translated; every other rule is ignored by this translation (Bash rules are applied by nax, below; write-tool rules can never widen a read-only profile).

| nax rule | opencode `permission` | Cursor `cli-config.json` | pi `--tools` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| none of these | `OPENCODE_READ_CONFIG` / `OPENCODE_REVIEW_CONFIG`, byte-identical | allow `Read(**)` | `read,grep,find,ls` |
| `Read` unconditional deny | drops `read` and `list` | `Read(**)` leaves allow and joins deny | drops `read` |
| `Glob` unconditional deny | drops `glob` | no change | drops `find` and `ls` |
| `Grep` unconditional deny | drops `grep` | no change | drops `grep` |

- **opencode** keeps today's `bash`: absent under `read` (no shell tool), `"ask"` under `review` (every command asks nax).

Integration targets:
- `ReadOnlyEnforcement` (`registry.ts`) — Baseline: `{ mode, disallowedTools, sessionOptions, launchEnv }`. Target: adds `policy: "opencode" | "cursor" | "pi" | undefined`, naming the rule-policy translator that builds the agent's launch env (opencode: `"opencode"`; cursor: `"cursor"`; pi: `"pi"`; others `undefined`). Cursor/pi selectors are set by US-004. Preserve policy when freezing registry records.
- `isReadOnlyProfile` (`capabilities.ts`) — Baseline: a module-local `const`. Target: exported, unchanged behaviour.
- `AcpBackendOptions` / `ResolvedAcpOptions` (`options.ts`) — Target: options gain `rules?: { allow?: AcpRule[]; deny?: AcpRule[]; ask?: AcpRule[] }` and `stateDir?: string` (absolute); resolved options gain `rules: AcpPermissionRules` (`NO_RULES` when unset) and `stateDir: string` (default `join(tmpdir(), "nax-agent-acp")`).
- `openAcpSession` (`open.ts`) — Baseline: `const env = { ...options.env, ...launchEnvFor(ctx.profile, options.entry) }`. Target: `const env = { ...options.env, ...(await policyLaunchEnv(ctx.profile, options)) }`, before the launch; a rejection refuses the open without launching.

Add `rules` and `stateDir` to the backend options with zod validation, add `policy` to `ReadOnlyEnforcement` (opencode `"opencode"`), export `isReadOnlyProfile`, create `src/client/rule-policy.ts` (`AcpRule`, `AcpPermissionRules`, `NO_RULES`, `opencodePermissionConfig`, `policyLaunchEnv`) and make `openAcpSession` launch with `policyLaunchEnv`. With no read-tool deny rule, opencode's launch env is byte-identical to today. Export the new types from `./client` and update the API snapshot.

Failure handling: `stateDir` is not absolute → `acpBackend()` throws `AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS`, path `stateDir`. A rule's `patterns` is empty or has a non-string element → `acpBackend()` throws `AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS`, path within `rules`. Preserve the existing schema error mapping.

Update the exact opencode registry expectation to include policy opencode and regenerate `packages/nax-agent-acp/api/nax-agent-acp.api.txt`. The seam ACs enter at `createAgentSession` with `acpBackend({ agent: "opencode", rules })` and assert the recorded launch env; use an explicit fake command and `_acpBackendDeps.launch`. Exercise relaunch after process exit so policy cannot disappear on reconnect.

**Scope** — In: rule/stateDir validation and normalization, policy discriminator, opencode translator, asynchronous pre-spawn env seam, public rule types and snapshot. Out: Cursor registration/model alias logic (US-001), Bash permission decisions/pi gate source (US-003), Cursor/pi policy implementation and disk writes (US-004), nax forwarding/discovery/docs (US-005), native matcher exports (US-006). Translating any Bash rule into an agent's own config, and `Mcp(...)`, path-scoped `Read(...)`/`Write(...)`, `Git`, `RunCommand` or `Exec` rules for any ACP agent.

**Interface** —
```ts
export interface AcpRule { readonly tool: string; readonly patterns: readonly string[] }
export interface AcpPermissionRules {
  readonly allow: readonly AcpRule[];
  readonly deny: readonly AcpRule[];
  readonly ask: readonly AcpRule[];
}
export const NO_RULES: AcpPermissionRules;
export function opencodePermissionConfig(profile: "none" | "read" | "review", rules: AcpPermissionRules): string;
export function policyLaunchEnv(profile: AgentSessionProfile, options: ResolvedAcpOptions): Promise<Readonly<Record<string, string>>>;
```
The subsequent US-004 extension adds cursorCliConfig and piToolArgs; they are not outputs of this story.

[integration] When opencode opens with profile read and no rules, then it launches with OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT equal to OPENCODE_READ_CONFIG.
[integration] When opencode opens with profile read, a Read deny rule and caller env.OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT equal to "{}", then it launches with the translated value, not "{}".
[integration] When an opencode read session with a Read deny rule relaunches after its agent process exits, then the relaunch carries the same OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT as the first launch.

userStories.title: Adjudicate unsandboxed ACP review shell requests with Bash rules
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let nax allow only operator-granted, lexically readable shell commands in review permission requests without an effective nax sandbox.

**Motivation** — The operator asked that read-only enforcement be configurable rather than a fixed harness, and nax already has the configuration surface: `resolvePermissions` turns `execution.permissions.<stage>` into `toolGrants`, `denyRules` and `askRules` on `ResolvedPermissions`, which every `OpenSessionOpts` carries, but the ACP path reads only the resolved mode.

**Approach** — Module `packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/shell-rules.ts` (US-003):

- **`shellCommandOf`**: for `pi`, a tool call of kind `other` whose `rawInput.method` is `"confirm"`, `rawInput.title` is `PI_SHELL_GATE_TITLE` and `rawInput.message` is a non-empty string yields that message; for `cursor`, a tool call of kind `execute` whose `title` is a non-empty string yields the title with one enclosing pair of backticks removed; for every other agent, a tool call of kind `execute` whose `rawInput.command` is a non-empty string yields it. Anything else yields `undefined`. The raw value is used (not the secret-masked display text).
- **`shellRuleVerdict`**: `lexBashCommand(command)`; `"deny"` when the lexer refuses, when it yields no segment, when any segment has a redirect, or when any token is opaque. A segment's argv is its token texts. A segment is allowed when the argv matches a pattern of some `Bash` rule in `rules.allow` and matches no pattern of any `Bash` rule in `rules.deny` or `rules.ask` (no person answers an ACP read-only session, so `ask` denies). Matching is nax's native argv matching, reused from nax-agent's public entry (US-006): a pattern matches when `matchesArgvPattern(compileArgvPattern(pattern), argv)` is true (each whitespace-separated pattern token is a glob matched against the argv token at the same position, and the pattern tokens are a prefix of argv), and the pattern `*` alone matches every segment. Native's payload checks (denied flags, path containment) are not applied to ACP commands. The verdict is `"allow"` only when every segment is allowed.
- `PI_SHELL_GATE_SOURCE` is the pi gate extension source: a pi extension that, on `tool_call` for tool `bash`, blocks the call when the session has no UI, else asks `ctx.ui.confirm(PI_SHELL_GATE_TITLE, command)` and blocks the call with reason `"nax: shell command rejected"` unless it returns true.

Integration targets:
- `PermissionContext` (`permissions.ts`) — Target: gains optional `agentName?: string` and `rules?: AcpPermissionRules` (absent: no Bash rule allows anything, and `shellCommandOf` uses the generic `rawInput.command` source), so existing callers and the permission tests that build context literals compile unchanged; `routerFor(ctx, secrets, entry)` in `backend.ts` gains the resolved options' `agentName` and `rules` (its call site already has `options` in scope) and fills both.
- `decidePermission` (`permissions.ts`), `review` branch — Baseline: kind `execute` with a sandbox policy allows, without one denies with `REVIEW_NO_SANDBOX_REASON`; every other kind denies. Target: unchanged when a sandbox policy is present. Without one: a request whose `shellCommandOf(agentName, toolCall)` is defined and whose `shellRuleVerdict(command, rules)` is `"allow"` is allowed with `SHELL_RULE_REASON` when the agent offered an allow-once option, and otherwise denied as today's missing-allow-once path does (`NO_ALLOW_ONCE_REASON`); a request with a defined command and a `"deny"` verdict, and an `execute` request with no derivable command, are denied with `REVIEW_NO_SANDBOX_REASON`; any other request (an `edit`, or kind `other` that is not the pi gate) is denied with `readOnlyReason("review")`, as today.

Symbols read, unchanged:
- `ResolvedPermissions` (`packages/nax-agent/src/permissions/types.ts`): `mode`, `toolGrants?`, `denyRules?`, `askRules?` (each `readonly ToolGrant[]`, a `ToolGrant` being `{ tool: string; patterns: readonly string[] }`, unconditional when `patterns` is exactly `["*"]`), and the required `bashApproval`.
- `compileArgvPattern(pattern)`, `matchesArgvPattern(compiled, argv)` and `CompiledPattern` (`packages/nax-agent/src/tools/policy-match.ts`): nax's native per-token prefix matching for `Bash(...)`/`Exec(...)` grants; exported from `@nathapp/nax-agent` by US-006.
- `lexBashCommand(command): BashLexResult` (exported from `@nathapp/nax-agent`): `{ kind: "ok"; segments }` or `{ kind: "refused"; ... }`; a `BashSegment` has `tokens: { text; opaque }[]` and `redirects: { operator; target; opaque }[]`.
- `describeToolCall` (`tool-display.ts`), `offeredOptions`, `rejectWith`, `REVIEW_NO_SANDBOX_REASON`, `REVIEW_EXECUTE_REASON` (`permissions.ts`).

Create `src/client/shell-rules.ts` (`SHELL_RULE_REASON`, `PI_SHELL_GATE_TITLE`, `PI_SHELL_GATE_SOURCE`, `shellCommandOf`, `shellRuleVerdict`). Add `agentName` and `rules` to `PermissionContext`, fill them in `routerFor`, and extend the `review` branch of `decidePermission` as the Design states. Profiles `none`, `read`, `full` and `ask`, and `review` with a sandbox policy, decide exactly as today.

Failure handling: a shell command the lexer refuses, or with a redirect or opaque token → `shellRuleVerdict` returns `"deny"`; the request is denied with `REVIEW_NO_SANDBOX_REASON`. Under `review`, an allow verdict but the agent offered no allow-once option → denied with `NO_ALLOW_ONCE_REASON` (today's path).

The seam ACs enter at `createAgentSession` with `acpBackend({ agent, rules })`, profile `review`, a fake turn that sends a permission request, and assert the recorded answer and the `approval_requested` reason. Use `_acpBackendDeps.launch`, explicit fake commands and existing event helpers. Test the source extension by writing it to a temporary module and importing/calling it, including hasUI false and non-bash events. US-003 adds shell-rules and its tests and changes only source files (permissions.ts, backend.ts); the new PermissionContext fields are optional, so the permission and elicitation tests that build context literals compile unchanged, and absent rules decide exactly as today.

**Scope** — In: raw command extraction, lexer/prefix matching, fail-closed deny/ask handling, exact reason/option selection, pi gate source and backend context propagation. Out: writing/loading pi gate and wrappers or Cursor policy files (US-004), translator/options infrastructure (US-002), nax forwarding (US-005), changing native matcher algorithms (US-006). An OS sandbox for opencode, Cursor or pi shell commands (pi's sandbox-runtime extension, or sandboxing the agent process): a follow-up issue; until then an allowed `review` command runs unsandboxed. Translating any Bash rule into an agent's own config, and `Mcp(...)`, path-scoped `Read(...)`/`Write(...)`, `Git`, `RunCommand` or `Exec` rules for any ACP agent.

**Interface** —
```ts
export const SHELL_RULE_REASON = "an operator Bash rule allows this command";
export const PI_SHELL_GATE_TITLE = "nax: run shell command";
/** Source of the pi extension that turns each bash call into a confirm prompt (written to disk by US-004). */
export const PI_SHELL_GATE_SOURCE: string;
export function shellCommandOf(agentName: string, toolCall: unknown): string | undefined;
export function shellRuleVerdict(command: string, rules: AcpPermissionRules): "allow" | "deny";
```

userStories.title: Enforce Cursor and pi read-only profiles with atomic launch policies
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enforce Cursor and pi none/read/review profiles through generated agent policies and a pi shell-gate wrapper prepared before spawn.

**Motivation** — nax#2372 asks for read-only support on every ACP agent.

**Approach** — Extend Module `packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/rule-policy.ts` (US-002, extended by US-004):

`policyLaunchEnv` returns `launchEnvFor(profile, entry)` unchanged for profiles `full` and `ask`, for entries whose `readOnly.policy` is `undefined`, and for custom agents. Otherwise it dispatches on `readOnly.policy`.

**Read-tool deny translation** (profiles `read` and `review`; under `none` the rules are ignored). Only an unconditional deny (`patterns: ["*"]`) of `Read`, `Glob` or `Grep` is translated; every other rule is ignored by this translation (Bash rules are applied by nax, below; write-tool rules can never widen a read-only profile).

| nax rule | opencode `permission` | Cursor `cli-config.json` | pi `--tools` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| none of these | `OPENCODE_READ_CONFIG` / `OPENCODE_REVIEW_CONFIG`, byte-identical | allow `Read(**)` | `read,grep,find,ls` |
| `Read` unconditional deny | drops `read` and `list` | `Read(**)` leaves allow and joins deny | drops `read` |
| `Glob` unconditional deny | drops `glob` | no change | drops `find` and `ls` |
| `Grep` unconditional deny | drops `grep` | no change | drops `grep` |

- **opencode** keeps today's `bash`: absent under `read` (no shell tool), `"ask"` under `review` (every command asks nax).
- **Cursor** `{"version":1,"permissions":{"allow":[...],"deny":[...]},"approvalMode":"allowlist"}`. `allow` is `["Read(**)"]`, or `[]` when Read is denied. `deny` is `Write(**)`, `Delete(**)`, `Mcp(*:*)`, `WebFetch(*)`, then `Shell(*)` under `read`, then `Read(**)` when Read is denied. Under `none`: allow `[]`, deny `Write(**)`, `Delete(**)`, `Mcp(*:*)`, `WebFetch(*)`, `Shell(*)`, `Read(**)`. Under `review` shell is unlisted, so every command asks nax.
- **pi** `piToolArgs` returns `["--no-tools"]` under `none`. Otherwise the list is built in the order `read,grep,find,ls` minus the denied tools; under `review`, when `rules.allow` holds any `Bash` rule, `bash` is appended and `["-e", gatePath]` is prepended, so every bash call goes through the nax shell gate. The result is `["--no-tools"]` only when the final list is empty, else `["--tools", "<list>"]`.

Policy files (US-004):

`src/client/policy-files.ts` exports `writeCursorPolicy(stateDir, content): Promise<string>`, `writePiFile(stateDir, name, content, mode): Promise<string>` and `_policyFilesDeps` (`mkdir`, `writeFile`, `rename`, `chmod`, from `node:fs/promises`; no Bun API in this package).

- **Content-addressed.** `<h>` is the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the file content. Cursor: `<stateDir>/cursor/<h>/cli-config.json`, returning the directory. pi: `<stateDir>/pi/<name>-<h><ext>` for the gate extension (`shell-gate`, `.ts`) and the wrapper (`wrapper`, `.sh`), returning the file path.
- **Atomic, every launch.** Each file is written to a temporary name in its target directory and renamed over the target, on every launch (Cursor rewrites its config itself, and a rewrite replaces a planted or half-written file). Directories are created recursively with mode `0o700`; `chmod` sets `0o600` on Cursor's config and the gate extension and `0o700` on the wrapper, on the temporary file before the rename.
- **Launch env.** Cursor: `{ CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR: <dir> }`. pi: the gate extension is written first (under `review` with a `Bash` allow rule), then the wrapper `#!/bin/sh
exec <pi> <args> "$@"
`, `<pi>` being the caller's `PI_ACP_PI_COMMAND` from `options.env` or else `pi`, and `<args>` `piToolArgs(...)`, every word single-quoted for `sh` (a `'` inside becomes `'\''`); env `{ PI_ACP_PI_COMMAND: <wrapper path> }`. opencode: `{ OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT: opencodePermissionConfig(profile, rules) }`, no file.
- The env is spread over the caller's, so a caller cannot weaken it.

Add `cursorCliConfig` and `piToolArgs` to `rule-policy.ts`, create `src/client/policy-files.ts` (`writeCursorPolicy`, `writePiFile`, `_policyFilesDeps`), and extend `policyLaunchEnv` for `policy: "cursor"` (`CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR`) and `policy: "pi"` (wrapper, plus the gate extension under `review` with a Bash allow rule, via `PI_ACP_PI_COMMAND`). Set the cursor entry's `policy` to `"cursor"` and give pi `readOnly: { mode: undefined, disallowedTools: [], sessionOptions: {}, launchEnv: {}, policy: "pi" }`.

Failure handling: a policy file cannot be written (any `_policyFilesDeps` call rejects) → open refused with `AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`, naming the path; the agent is never launched. Write policy files on every launch, including resume/reconnect through openAcpSession; no file operation for full/ask.

Existing test changes: registry.test.ts's cursor entry expected readOnly gains policy cursor; the pi test titled "no read-only enforcement" now asserts the new readOnly record; the invariant becomes "a mode, a launch env for none, read and review, or a policy". capabilities.test.ts's readOnlyFor none example switches from pi to a custom agent (no registry entry), keeping the invariant that an agent without enforcement yields undefined. backend-permissions.test.ts's pi read/none refusal example switches to a custom agent spec, keeping that invariant. The seam ACs enter at `createAgentSession` with `acpBackend({ agent: "cursor", rules, stateDir })` or `acpBackend({ agent: "pi", rules, stateDir })` and assert the recorded launch env. Use temporary state directories and the in-memory fake through `_acpBackendDeps.launch`, never a real adapter. Pi review round trips must prove its kind other confirm gate reaches US-003's rule decision.

**Scope** — In: Cursor/pi translators, content-addressed atomic files and permissions, POSIX quoting, pi extension/wrapper launch integration, registry enforcement and unsupported-custom-agent regressions. Out: Cursor alias registration (US-001), changing opencode rule semantics/options normalization (US-002), changing shell verdict algorithms/gate source (US-003), nax forwarding/discovery/docs (US-005), matcher exports (US-006). An OS sandbox for opencode, Cursor or pi shell commands (pi's sandbox-runtime extension, or sandboxing the agent process): a follow-up issue; until then an allowed `review` command runs unsandboxed. A repository's own `.cursor/cli.json` permission rules, which Cursor merges and whose allow rules override the isolated config's denies (probed); nax does not detect or refuse them (accepted 2026-10-17). Cursor hooks from the operator's own Cursor configuration, which still run and can rewrite a command before nax sees it (probed: `ls` arrived as `rtk ls -la`). Stopping pi's installed extensions from loading (their tools are filtered by `--tools`; their code still runs). Removing stale content-addressed policy files under the state directory, and protecting a state directory owned by another user: the trust boundary is the state directory's owner. Windows: the pi wrapper is a POSIX `sh` script. Translating any Bash rule into an agent's own config, and `Mcp(...)`, path-scoped `Read(...)`/`Write(...)`, `Git`, `RunCommand` or `Exec` rules for any ACP agent.

**Interface** —
```ts
export function cursorCliConfig(profile: "none" | "read" | "review", rules: AcpPermissionRules): string; // US-004
export function piToolArgs(profile: "none" | "read" | "review", rules: AcpPermissionRules, gatePath: string): readonly string[]; // US-004
export function policyLaunchEnv(profile: AgentSessionProfile, options: ResolvedAcpOptions): Promise<Readonly<Record<string, string>>>;
```
`writeCursorPolicy(stateDir, content): Promise<string>` returns the Cursor directory; `writePiFile(stateDir, name, content, mode): Promise<string>` returns the pi file path. `_policyFilesDeps` exposes `mkdir`, `writeFile`, `rename`, `chmod` from `node:fs/promises`.

userStories.title: Forward nax permission rules to ACP and expose Cursor
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Connect nax's existing resolved stage rules to ACP options and make Cursor discoverable through nax's agent registry.

**Motivation** — The operator asked that read-only enforcement be configurable rather than a fixed harness, and nax already has the configuration surface: `resolvePermissions` turns `execution.permissions.<stage>` into `toolGrants`, `denyRules` and `askRules` on `ResolvedPermissions`, which every `OpenSessionOpts` carries, but the ACP path reads only the resolved mode.

**Approach** — nax wiring (US-005):

- `backendOptions` passes `rules: { allow: toolGrants ?? [], deny: denyRules ?? [], ask: askRules ?? [] }` from `opts.resolvedPermissions` and `stateDir: join(globalConfigDir(), "acp")`.
- `KNOWN_AGENT_NAMES` and `ENTRIES` gain `cursor` (`binary: "cursor-agent"`, `displayName: "Cursor Agent (ACP)"`, tiers `fast`/`balanced`/`powerful`, `maxContextTokens: 200_000`).
- `docs/guides/permissions.md` gains an "ACP agents" section: read-tool deny translation per agent, the Bash-rule decision under `review` for agents without nax's sandbox (Claude keeps its sandboxed review), that an allowed command runs on the host unsandboxed, that Cursor matches what its own hooks rewrote, and the pi gate. `docs/guides/configuration.md` links it.

Integration targets:
- `backendOptions` (`packages/nax/src/agents/acp/open-context.ts`) — Target: adds `rules` from `opts.resolvedPermissions` and `stateDir: join(globalConfigDir(), "acp")`.
- `KNOWN_AGENT_NAMES` (`packages/nax/src/agents/registry.ts`) and the ACP `ENTRIES` table (`packages/nax/src/agents/acp/entries.ts`) — Target: both gain `cursor`.

`backendOptions` passes `rules` from `opts.resolvedPermissions` and `stateDir` under `globalConfigDir()`. Add `cursor` to `KNOWN_AGENT_NAMES`, the ACP entries table and the `agent.acp` config description. Update the `profile-map.ts` header comment (pi is no longer refused `read`). Document ACP agents in `docs/guides/permissions.md` and link it from `docs/guides/configuration.md`.

Symbols read, unchanged:
- `ResolvedPermissions` (`packages/nax-agent/src/permissions/types.ts`): `mode`, `toolGrants?`, `denyRules?`, `askRules?` (each `readonly ToolGrant[]`, a `ToolGrant` being `{ tool: string; patterns: readonly string[] }`, unconditional when `patterns` is exactly `["*"]`), and the required `bashApproval`.
- `globalConfigDir()` (`packages/nax/src/config/paths`).

The seam: `backendOptions` passes rules into `acpBackend`; its ACs call `backendOptions` with `OpenSessionOpts` carrying rules and pass the result to `acpBackend` (the open path from `SessionManager.openSession` to `backendOptions` is unchanged). Do not import NaxConfig or perform a second permission resolution inside the ACP adapter. Preserve profile mapping, env, model/effort, process hooks, inheritEnv and deadline values. Forward rules without silently filtering malformed entries: the existing acpBackend option validator remains responsible for rejecting an empty-pattern deny rule received through backendOptions, as asserted by this story's negative-path integration check. The safe-profile review-config AC validates backend option compatibility only; it does not authorize changing acpProfileFor to widen safe mode.

`packages/nax/test/unit/agents/acp/entries.test.ts` — the test asserting the sorted ACP_AGENT_NAMES equals the five current names gains cursor.
`packages/nax/test/unit/agents/acp/open-context.test.ts` — US-005's backendOptions acceptance tests are added; the existing tests use partial matching and do not change.

Documentation must distinguish read-tool deny translation (opencode Read removes read/list, Glob removes glob, Grep removes grep; Cursor only Read removes its read allowance; pi Read removes read, Glob removes find/ls, Grep removes grep) from Bash decisions (every segment must match an allow, deny/ask veto, redirects/opaque/unreadable syntax refuse). None/read never run shell. No Bash allow is translated into agent config. With no rules configured existing supported-agent behavior is unchanged. Describe the accepted Cursor repository-config/hook and pi extension trust boundaries without promising an OS sandbox.

**Scope** — In: nax backend option forwarding, canonical global state path, Cursor metadata/discovery/config description, header correction and the assigned root documentation edits. Out: ACP implementation and policy-file changes (US-001–004), native matcher exports/API snapshot (US-006), altering resolvePermissions or widening profiles. Read-tool rule translation for Claude, codex and gemini; Bash-rule decisions for them apply only where they send an `execute` permission request without nax's sandbox. Updating `.nax/mono/packages/nax-agent-acp/context.md` for Cursor and pi: a manual step after merge, since `.nax/` is read-only to the run.

**Interface** — Existing `backendOptions(agent: AcpAgentName, opts: OpenSessionOpts, onProcess?: AcpProcessHooks): AcpBackendOptions` remains the seam. Its target additions are `rules: { allow: toolGrants ?? [], deny: denyRules ?? [], ask: askRules ?? [] }` and `stateDir: join(globalConfigDir(), "acp")`; `acpEntry("cursor")` returns `{ agent: "cursor", binary: "cursor-agent", displayName: "Cursor Agent (ACP)", supportedTiers: ["fast", "balanced", "powerful"], maxContextTokens: 200_000 }`.

Goal and completion: close #2372 by registering cursor-agent acp, enforcing none/read/review for Cursor and pi, translating only unconditional read-tool denies for rule-capable agents, and applying operator Bash rules in nax to unsandboxed review permission requests. Completion requires the six binding stories, public matcher and rule-type exports with API snapshots, fake-backed session seam assertions, nax rule forwarding and Cursor discovery, and operator documentation. No production implementation or live-agent verification is part of this PRD-generation task.

Navigation and architecture: codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host; findings below come from direct repository reads and searches. This is an enhancement to existing TypeScript ESM packages, not greenfield. packages/nax-agent-acp/package.json:7 exposes ./client and ./server; packages/nax-agent/package.json:7 exposes the root, ./internal and ./mcp. The ACP client must import nax-agent only through @nathapp/nax-agent, never its internal or deep paths; nax must import ACP only through @nathapp/nax-agent-acp/client. No nax-ai change or new dependency is needed. Shipped nax-agent and ACP code is Node-compatible, uses #src aliases and .ts relative imports, and must not introduce Bun APIs. Tests use bun:test plus existing Node vitest contracts. Read docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:14 and :159 for convention and package-boundary references before implementation. Keep the binding dependency graph: US-001, US-002 and US-006 have no dependencies; US-003 follows all three; US-004 follows US-001/002/003; US-005 follows all other stories. US-001 and US-002 share registry.ts, capabilities.ts and open.ts despite independent logical dependencies: integrate their additive edits without overwriting each other.

US-001 impact: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/registry.ts:10 has the five-name AcpAgentName union, :31 defines ReadOnlyEnforcement, :59 explicitly reconstructs frozen enforcement records, :105 begins registry data, and :186 currently registers pi without enforcement. Add Cursor after codex in registry order and ensure freezeReadOnly retains the new policy field when US-002 lands; otherwise dispatch will silently lose its selector. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/options.ts:90 hardcodes the zod agent enum independently of the union. Authentication env is taken from entry.authEnv by options.ts:131 and filtered through buildAgentEnv; adding CURSOR_API_KEY there keeps unrelated ambient variables excluded. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/capabilities.ts:96 flattens select groups, :106 finds model options, :135 and :140 resolve enforcement/mode. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/open.ts:271 applies the mode, :285 bounds existing model refusal labels, :305 requires exact config-option or legacy model offers today. Resolve Cursor aliases before both lookups; config-category model values take precedence over legacy IDs when any are present. Ambiguity must name every matching ID safely, not silently select a reasoning/context variant. Important baseline mismatch: text.ts:10 defines MIN_SECRET_LENGTH as 8 and :30 scrubSecrets ignores shorter values, but US-001 explicitly requires hiding SECRET1 (seven characters). The AC is authoritative: ambiguity errors must hide that value as well as using cleanLabel, without changing shared cleanLabel behavior for unrelated callers. Cursor mode ask is advisory, not the security boundary; Cursor policy enforcement arrives in US-004, and plan must never be substituted. Tests: test/unit/client/backend-gemini.test.ts:239 covers config-option precedence and legacy model failures, test/fixtures/fake-agent/script.ts:105 defines FakeScript with legacy models, :149 defines CLAUDE_CONFIG_OPTIONS. Extend that fixture with CURSOR_CONFIG_OPTIONS without changing existing exports. Registry exact equality and five-name assertions are at test/unit/client/registry.test.ts:12; the Node name count is test/node/registry.test.ts:10.

US-002 impact: options.ts:30 defines AcpBackendOptions, :55 resolved options, :90 strict schema and :159 resolveAcpOptions. Existing validation converts the first zod issue to AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS with a dotted context path; retain allowUnsandboxed validation precedence. Add optional rules/stateDir, normalize missing lists to NO_RULES and default stateDir to join(tmpdir(), "nax-agent-acp"). capabilities.ts:71 currently has a local isReadOnlyProfile and :148 launchEnvFor; expose the helper unchanged. registry.ts:82-91 serializes the current opencode constants in deterministic insertion order. Translation must preserve these exact strings unless an unconditional Read/Glob/Grep deny changes them; Bash and write grants must never widen agent policy. open.ts:102 is the common spawn path, with env composition at :115 before launch. Await policyLaunchEnv before launching, preserving enforcement-env precedence. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/backend.ts:155 connect calls openAcpSession for new and restored sessions, and :263 reconnect calls connect again, so changing this single launch seam covers open/resume/reconnect. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/index.ts:11 is the named public client barrel; export AcpRule/AcpPermissionRules here and regenerate api/nax-agent-acp.api.txt. Tests: backend-opencode.test.ts:78 opens through createAgentSession, :108 reads recorded launch env, :181 covers reconnect, :140 and :155 pin existing config bytes and caller-env override. backend-reconnect.test.ts:90 provides the broader lifecycle regression pattern.

US-003 impact: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/permissions.ts:45 defines PermissionContext, :72 selects only offered *_once options, :99 rejects locally, and :112 decides requests. Current review behavior at :140 denies non-execute, denies execute without a sandbox, and allows sandboxed execute with REVIEW_EXECUTE_REASON. Preserve cancellation, network-policy handling and all other profiles. Add optional agentName/rules so current literal context callers remain source-compatible. backend.ts:135 routerFor currently forwards profile/asks/secrets/cwd and only gives an embedder sandbox to entries with preApproval; :164 has resolved options in scope for forwarding identity/rules. Do not accidentally treat an opencode/Cursor/pi embedder sandbox as effective: those agents never receive it. Tool-display.ts:101 commandSource currently extracts generic rawInput.command only for sanitized display, :107 describeToolCall masks and caps it. The new shellCommandOf must read raw agent-specific fields separately, while approval events retain the existing sanitized display path. Cursor's title is the post-hook command, pi is recognized only by the exact confirm gate shape, and absent agentName uses generic execute/rawInput.command. Never decide from secret-masked or truncated command text. packages/nax-agent/src/permissions/bash-lex.ts:25-64 defines tokens/redirects/segments and :105 lexBashCommand refuses unsupported constructs; use it unchanged, rejecting redirects, opaque tokens, zero segments and all lexer refusals. packages/nax-agent/src/tools/policy-match.ts:96 and :106 implement per-token glob prefix matching: a prefix can leave trailing argv unconstrained; do not replace it with whole-command regex matching or native payload containment checks. PI_SHELL_GATE_SOURCE is executed extension code and needs an actual temp-module import test, not a string-content-only assertion. backend-opencode.test.ts:123 has the execute permission step and :201 proves a non-preApproval agent does not gain the embedder sandbox.

US-004 impact: extend the US-002 rule-policy module and consume US-003 gate constants/source. Files must be content-addressed, rewritten atomically every launch, and chmodded on temporary files before rename; deterministic final paths enable sharing without trusting previously written content. Use node:crypto SHA-256 and node:fs/promises through _policyFilesDeps, not Bun. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/default-model.ts:67 provides a same-directory temp-write/rename precedent, but policy files have their own prescribed four-operation seam and replacement semantics. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/errors.ts:54 provides backendUnavailable for typed failures naming the path. Any mkdir/writeFile/chmod/rename failure must reject before launch. Pi wrapper quoting must preserve an executable path containing apostrophes as one shell word and forward "$@" unchanged; never treat PI_ACP_PI_COMMAND as arbitrary shell source. Write the gate before the wrapper only for review with a Bash allow rule, append bash only in that case, and never enable shell for none/read. Full/ask must retain existing env semantics and perform no policy-file operations. Existing registry tests at :34 assert pi has no enforcement and :194 require a mode or launch env; replace these with policy-aware expectations. test/unit/client/capabilities.test.ts:167 and backend-permissions.test.ts:138 currently use pi as an unsupported read-only example; switch those to a custom agent so the fail-closed invariant survives pi support. A repository's own `.cursor/cli.json` permission rules, which Cursor merges and whose allow rules override the isolated config's denies (probed); nax does not detect or refuse them (accepted 2026-10-17).
